brow: Aggregated snapshot · open-source compilation · not official reporting
editionNote: Evening edition. It covers the 24 hours to 17:10 CEST on 23 October; new research covers 05:10 CEST to 17:10 CEST on 23 October, items from the previous edition still inside the 24 hours were carried, and stories with new developments are marked as follow-ups.

theaters.heading: Battlefield, long-range strikes, and peace diplomacy in Russia's war on Ukraine

items.title: White House Says Russia and Ukraine Agree to a Local Truce in Oleshky
items.lede: The ceasefire, meant to let in aid and prepare an evacuation of mostly elderly residents, starts on 29 October, and each family's wishes will be respected, the First Lady said.

sections.text: The White House said on 23 October that Russia and Ukraine had agreed, through First Lady Melania Trump, to halt all military action in Oleshky, in Russian-occupied southern Ukraine across the Dnipro from Kherson, from 29 October [1]. The pause is meant to let humanitarian aid in and prepare a civilian evacuation through a designated passage, with civilian teams from both countries visiting residents [1][2]. Newsmax said its cameras would have exclusive access to document the effort, CNBC reported [2]. The release put the remaining population at 1,700 to 2,000, mostly elderly, with about 50 children, against about 24,000 before the war [1]. No Kremlin or Ukrainian government statement on the terms was found by the cutoff.

Confidence is high that the White House announced the deal, because the release was read directly and CNBC reports it. Confidence on Russian and Ukrainian acceptance is moderate, because neither government's own statement was found.

items.title: Strike on a Chernihiv Enterprise Kills One and Injures 25 in Northern Ukraine
items.lede: Eight victims were taken to hospital and people were briefly trapped under rubble, the city's military chief said, after Russia also hit a delivery depot.

sections.text: A Russian strike on an enterprise in Chernihiv, Ukraine, on 23 October killed one person and injured 25, city military administration head Dmytro Bryzhynskyi said [3]. He said 16 people were treated at the scene and eight taken to hospital, and that two enterprises had been hit, with people initially trapped under rubble [3]. He also reported an attack on a Nova Poshta delivery terminal in the north of the city [3]. No Russian statement on the target was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is high on the toll, because the city head gave it on record. Confidence on the target is low, because the enterprise was not named and no second outlet was found.

items.title: Mariupol Defenders Among 270 Ukrainian Soldiers Freed in a Swap With Russia
items.lede: Five survivors of the 2022 Olenivka prison blast came home in the first exchange in two months, and Moscow said its 270 returnees were waiting in Belarus.

sections.text: Ukraine and Russia each released 270 prisoners of war on 23 October, the first exchange in two months, President Zelensky said [4]. Most of the Ukrainians returning had been captured in the siege of Mariupol in spring 2022, including Azov fighters, border guards, and troops from the Ground Forces, Navy, and Air Assault Forces, and five survived the July 2022 Olenivka prison blast [4]. Ukraine's prisoner coordination headquarters said many had been convicted on sham charges in Russian captivity, and Zelensky and the headquarters said nine civilians also came home [4]. Russia's Defence Ministry said its freed soldiers were in Belarus and would be flown home after medical and psychological care [5]. It was the 11th reported exchange of 2026 [4].

Confidence is high on the numbers, because Kyiv and Moscow give the same figure and two outlets report it. Confidence on the civilian count is moderate, because Ukrainian officials first gave seven and later nine.

items.title: Russia Hits Ukraine's Power Grid in Eight Regions, Cutting Supply to Over 500,000
items.lede: One DTEK thermal plant stopped generating and eight civilians died nationwide over the past day, as 176 drones flew at the country overnight.

sections.text: Russia launched 176 long-range drones, 92 of them jet-powered, at Ukraine overnight into 23 October, and air defences downed 140, with impacts at 19 locations, Ukraine's Air Force said [6][7]. Grid operator Ukrenergo reported power cuts in Zhytomyr, Donetsk, Khmelnytskyi, Volyn, Kharkiv, Poltava, Rivne, and Mykolaiv regions, and the Energy Ministry put those left without power above 500,000 [7][8]. DTEK said one of its thermal plants stopped generating after the attack, without naming it [7][8]. In Volyn alone almost 105,000 customers lost power and one person was hurt [9]. A daytime drone strike on an energy site in Lviv region later cut power to 175 settlements [10]. Regional authorities counted eight civilians killed and 67 wounded across the country over the past day [7].

Confidence is high on the drone count and the outages, because the Air Force, Ukrenergo, and DTEK are on record and two outlets agree. Confidence on the national casualty total is moderate, because it is a tally of regional reports.

items.title: Drones Set Russia's Azot Chemical Plant in Perm Region on Fire, Media Say
items.lede: Russia's Defence Ministry claimed 443 drones downed overnight, including over Perm, while the nitric acid made there supplies the country's explosives factories.

sections.text: Drones struck the Azot chemical plant in Berezniki, Perm region, Russia, on the morning of 23 October, and the plant was on fire, the Telegram channel ASTRA said in an OSINT analysis relayed by Ukrinform [11]. Russia's Defence Ministry said it destroyed 443 Ukrainian drones overnight and mentioned air defence activity over Perm region, without reporting damage [11][8]. The Uralchem plant makes ammonia, nitric acid, and ammonium nitrate, and nitric acid feeds Russian explosives and powder plants, Ukrinform said [11]. ASTRA reported an earlier attack on the site on 11 September [11]. No Ukrainian military claim was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate on the strike and fire, because they rest on one OSINT channel relayed by Ukrinform. Confidence is high on the 443-drone figure, because CNBC also reports it.

items.title: Kremlin Sets Three-Way Talks With Ukraine and the US for Abu Dhabi in November
items.lede: Russia's spokesman Peskov named the first half of November, while Putin insisted the goal is a final deal rather than a short pause in fighting.

sections.text: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said on 23 October that the next round of talks between Russia, Ukraine, and the US was planned for the first half of November in Abu Dhabi, in a trilateral format [5]. It would be the first such round since talks lapsed earlier this year [5]. In a state television interview aired late on 22 October, President Vladimir Putin said the talks must aim at security for Ukraine and Russia under a final agreement, not a short truce [12][8]. Zelensky told CNN he was ready for a ceasefire but needed strong security guarantees [8].

Confidence is high on Peskov's and Putin's statements, because AFP, Reuters, and CNBC carry them. Confidence on the November date is moderate, because no Ukrainian or US confirmation of the venue was found.

items.title: Russian Strike on Lozova Market Kills Two and Wounds 36 in Ukraine's Kharkiv Region
items.lede: Four of the wounded are in critical condition, the town's chief said, after the lunchtime hit on a crowded bazaar also damaged a church and some 200 flats.

sections.text: A Russian strike on the central market in Lozova, Kharkiv region, Ukraine, at lunchtime on 22 October killed two people and injured 36, Lozova community head Serhii Zelensky said that evening; four of the injured were critical and 29 moderately serious [13]. He said the blast also hit the Holy Smolensk Church and blew out windows in nearly 200 flats of a nearby high-rise [13]. Reuters, citing regional officials, also put the toll at two dead and 36 injured [14]. Regional governor Oleh Syniehubov had earlier given 17 injured, and on 21 October Russian attacks on Kharkiv city and 11 settlements killed one woman and injured 15 [15][16]. No Russian statement on the Lozova target was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is high on the toll, because the local authority and Reuters agree. Confidence on what Russia aimed at is low, because no account of the target was found.

items.title: Shahed Drone Hits a Home Near Zhytomyr, Wounding Nine Including Two Children in Ukraine
items.lede: Two of the injured went to the regional hospital, the governor said, as Russian drones hit the region for a second day running.

sections.text: A Russian Shahed drone struck a private house in the Zhytomyr community, Ukraine, on the evening of 22 October, injuring nine people, two of them children, Zhytomyr regional governor Vitalii Bunechko said [17]. Two of the injured were taken to the regional hospital, and rescuers, medics, and the Red Cross worked at the site [17]. The region's energy sites and homes had also been hit by drones the previous day, Ukrinform said [17]. No Russian statement on the target was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is high on the casualty count, because it comes on record from the regional governor. Confidence on what was targeted is low, because no account of the aim was found.

items.title: Russian Drone Sets a Commuter Train Ablaze in Ukraine's Kharkiv
items.lede: Nobody was hurt as rescuers put out the blaze in the lead car, the emergency service said, a month after a train strike nearby killed one man.

sections.text: A Russian drone struck a passenger electric train in Kharkiv, Ukraine, during the day on 22 October, setting its lead car on fire, the State Emergency Service in Kharkiv region said [18]. Rescuers put out the fire despite the threat of further shelling, and no one was injured [18]. President Zelensky had earlier reported the strike on the train [18]. A Russian strike on a train in the same region on 18 September killed one man and injured eight [18]. No Russian comment was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is high on the strike and the fire, because the emergency service and the president both reported it. No independent imagery was checked this run.

theaters.heading: Sabotage, drones, cyber, disinformation, and espionage targeting European states

items.title: Romania Blames Russia After a Drone Sinks a Cargo Ship Off Constanta
items.lede: One sailor died and three were missing, President Nicusor Dan said, in at least the seventh hit on merchant shipping near NATO's Black Sea coast in two weeks.

sections.text: A drone strike sank the Comoros-flagged cargo ship Khoryv about 13 nautical miles off Romania's port of Constanta, just outside Romanian territorial waters, on 23 October, Reuters reported [1]. Romania's naval authority said nine of the 13 Ukrainian and Azeri crew were rescued, one body was recovered, and three were missing [1][2]. President Nicusor Dan called it part of Russia's escalation in its war in Ukraine [1]. European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen condemned another Russian escalation in the Black Sea [3]. Reuters counts at least seven cargo ships hit off Romania and Bulgaria in two weeks, with some 30 sailors dead or missing, mostly near the Sulina Canal, Ukraine's main Danube export route [1]. No Russian response was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is high on the sinking and toll, because Romanian authorities and Reuters agree. Confidence on Russian responsibility is moderate, because it rests on Romania's attribution.

items.title: European Public Broadcasters Map About 100 Russia-Linked Hybrid Incidents
items.lede: The tally covers April to mid-October across 17 countries and excludes cyber operations, with the Black Sea the newest front, Belgium's RTBF said.

sections.text: Journalists in the Eurovision News Spotlight network documented about 100 incidents in 17 European countries between 1 April and 15 October 2026 that officials or media linked to Russia, Belgium's RTBF reported on 23 October [4]. The map covers physical attacks and recruited proxy agents and leaves out cyber attacks, influence operations, and espionage [4]. The latest cluster is in the Black Sea, where drones hit merchant ships off Romania and Bulgaria, with two deaths confirmed and at least ten missing since early October [4].
Confidence is moderate on the count, because it rests on attributions by officials and media that the project compiled rather than on court findings.

items.title: Ukraine's Military Intelligence Warns of Russian False-Flag Sabotage in the EU
items.lede: Kaliningrad, Russian Orthodox Church sites, and areas with Russian-speaking communities were among the possible targets listed, though the agency named no specific plots.

sections.text: Ukraine's Defence Intelligence (HUR) said on 23 October that Russia is preparing false-flag operations in Central and Eastern Europe, including the Baltic states, to blame on Ukraine [5][6]. HUR named two aims: discrediting Ukraine's forces to cut foreign support and intimidating European governments and societies [6]. Listed possible targets were critical infrastructure and border areas, the Kaliningrad exclave, areas with Russian-speaking populations, Russian Orthodox Church properties, and sites tied to Russian history [6]. HUR did not name specific planned attacks [6]. Russia denies involvement in sabotage in Europe [6].
Confidence is high that HUR made the warning, because two outlets carry it. Confidence on the alleged plans is low, because HUR is a party to the war and named no specific plots.

items.title: Britain Proposes 14-Year Terms for Saboteurs of Undersea Cables and Pipelines
items.lede: A Telegraph analysis counts more than 500 cases of Russian trawlers loitering over British cables in four and a half years, as London opens a 12-week consultation.

sections.text: The UK government published a White Paper on 22 October proposing new offences for intentional, reckless, or negligent damage to undersea telecoms and energy infrastructure, with prison terms of up to 14 years for intentional damage and unlimited fines for ship owners [7]. Telecoms Minister Ian Murray cited suspicious Russian activity around undersea infrastructure, and the department recalled an April exposure of a covert Russian submarine operation near UK waters [7]. A 12-week consultation now opens [7]. The Telegraph, citing Global Fishing Watch tracking data, reported more than 500 incidents over four and a half years in which Russian trawlers operated above cables linking Britain with Europe and the US, Turkey's Anadolu Agency said [8]. Britain's Defence Ministry said it was clear-eyed about the Russian threat [8]. Russian State Duma deputy Svetlana Zhurova told Lenta.ru the trawler story was aimed at gullible people and London should look into the Nord Stream blasts instead [9].

Confidence is high on the proposals, because they come from the government's own release. Confidence on the trawler count is moderate, because it rests on one newspaper analysis relayed by a wire agency. A senior Duma deputy dismissed the trawler account as a British fabrication; no Kremlin or Foreign Ministry response was found.

theaters.heading: Politics, security, and defense across the EU and NATO's European members

items.title: Gunman Kills One and Wounds Five in Drive-By Shootings West of Paris
items.lede: France's anti-terrorism prosecutor took the case as possible racially motivated terrorism, and Nuñez said the suspect, now in custody, fired for almost 15 minutes.

sections.text: A gunman fired from a car at people in Trappes and nearby La Verrière, west of Paris, France, on Friday morning, killing one person and wounding five, three seriously, the BBC reported [1]. A 12-year-old girl is among the wounded [1][2]. The suspect, a 39-year-old man, was arrested, and the National Anti-Terrorism Prosecutor's Office is investigating murder and attempted murder "in connection with a terrorist enterprise" based on the victims' race, ethnicity, nation, or religion [3][2]. Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said "it's clearly a terrorist crime" [1]. Trappes mayor Ali Rabeh said the man fired at a petrol station, a medical centre, and a playground, and described a "racist, probably Islamophobic" overtone; the prosecutor urged caution on the victims' identities [1]. The suspect was known to police but not to France's intelligence services, the BBC reported, citing local media [1]. No motive was announced by the cutoff.

Confidence is high on the attack and the investigation, because the prosecutor and minister spoke on record and the BBC, Politico, and NOS report them; casualty counts differ slightly between outlets.

items.title: Britain Urges Households to Keep Three Days of Water and Food
items.lede: The UK advice covers storms and cyberattacks, El País said, and it arrived as Storm Austen cut power to thousands of homes in south-west England.

sections.text: The UK government's Be Ready campaign tells households to keep supplies for three days [4], including three litres of drinking water per person per day and food that needs no fridge or cooking [5]. El País reported on Friday that the government also advises spare phone batteries and a battery radio, following similar guidance in France, the Netherlands, and Ireland [5]. The paper said British intelligence has warned for weeks of sabotage and hybrid attacks by states such as Russia and Iran [5]. Storm Austen left thousands of homes in south-west England without power on Friday [5]. The campaign page was last updated on 21 October [4].
Confidence is high on the guidance, because the government page states it; the threat framing rests on El País.

items.title: Austria Expels Four Russian Diplomats Over Spying
items.lede: Three work at Moscow's embassy in Vienna and one at its OSCE delegation, and Russia's foreign ministry promised an unavoidable response.

sections.text: Austria's foreign ministry expelled four Russian diplomats for activities "incompatible with their diplomatic status", wording used for espionage, NOS reported [6]. Three work at the Russian embassy in Vienna and the fourth is a member of Russia's delegation to the OSCE, which is based in the city [6]. Russia's foreign ministry said a response would "inevitably" follow, NOS reported [6]. In May a former officer of Austria's domestic intelligence service was jailed for four years for spying for Russia [6]. No statement from the Austrian ministry itself was read by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate, because one major Dutch outlet reports the expulsions, citing the Austrian and Russian ministries.

items.title: Marseille Drops Saturday Transit Halt as Nîmes Adds a Curfew for Minors
items.lede: France's curfew map keeps growing before the 24 October protests, with Paris nights restricted to Monday and Lyon publishing its exact protest-ban perimeter.

sections.text: The Paris police prefecture in France keeps its 23:00 to 06:00 curfew around Place de la République and Les Halles every night until Monday 26 October, for adults and minors [7][8][9]. On Friday the Bouches-du-Rhône prefect reversed his plan to suspend Marseille's public transport on Saturday, saying service will be run according to the public-order situation, while the adult curfew and the department-wide protest ban stay [10]. The Rhône prefecture published the order behind Saturday's Lyon protest ban, covering the Presqu'île, where more than 150 shops were damaged, the old town, the 6th district, and part of the 3rd [10]. The Gard prefect banned protests in parts of Nîmes and Alès and set a curfew for minors in central Nîmes from 22:00 Saturday to 05:00 Sunday [10]. Toulouse keeps a curfew in part of its centre until 05:00 Sunday [9]. Limoges will shut museums, a library, and sports sites on Saturday under prefecture orders [10].
Confidence is high, because the orders come from prefectures and are reported by CNews, franceinfo, and L'Internaute.

items.title: French Unions Reject a New Paris March Route and Vow to Start at Bastille
items.lede: French unions in Bordeaux also filed a city-centre route against the prefect's wishes, while the CGT wants the 5 November strike to spread to every workplace.

sections.text: The Ile-de-France union alliance in France said on Friday it refuses a new route from Porte de Vincennes to Porte d'Italie that the Paris police prefecture wants to impose, a day after both sides agreed on a Bastille to Nation march [10]. CGT Paris co-general secretary Karl Ghazi told AFP the new route was "impossible to secure" [10]. In Bordeaux, the CGT, FSU, and FO filed a 14:00 route from Place de la Bourse through the city centre, after the prefect asked them to avoid it [11]. A union asked the Bouches-du-Rhône prefect to allow a march in Marseille despite the ban, and the Somme prefect approved a union march in Amiens from 14:00 to 18:00 [10]. In Orléans, the march against the National Rally congress, where 20,000 to 30,000 people are expected, was rerouted away from the centre [10]. The CGT called on 22 October for workplace meetings to generalise the 5 November strike called by the national union alliance [12].
Confidence is high on the union positions, because the unions stated them on record to AFP and CNews and Sud Ouest report them; the Paris route remains in dispute.

items.title: France Deploys 70,000 Police and Gendarmes With Armoured Vehicles for Saturday
items.lede: Interior Minister Nuñez cited many online calls for looting from the far left after Macron chaired a defence council on security.

sections.text: French Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez told a press conference on Friday that 70,000 police and gendarmes will be deployed on Saturday, including RAID, GIGN, and BRI elite units, about 20 Centaure armoured vehicles, 15 water cannon, and helicopters [10]. He said there were "many calls" on social media from the ultra-left and radical far left to commit violence and looting [10]. Euronews had reported about 80,000 on Thursday, and Al Jazeera, with AFP, put the increase at 20 percent over last weekend [13][14]. President Emmanuel Macron chaired a defence council in the morning and received school-student organisations at the Elysée at 15:00; he is due at a Paris police barracks in the 19th district at 19:00 [10]. Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu visited Limoges, whose town hall was set on fire on 17 October, and Nuñez went to Orléans before Saturday's National Rally congress [10]. The student union UNEF said its Saturday rallies would go ahead despite Macron's rule that only union marches are allowed [14]. No list of the defence council's decisions was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is high on the deployment, because Nuñez gave the figure on record and CNews reports it; Euronews's earlier 80,000 figure conflicts.

items.title: France Jails 232 People and Opens 263 Organised-Gang Cases Over the Riots
items.lede: Justice Minister Darmanin said 1,144 people have been brought before prosecutors, and investigators have since arrested nearly 500 more suspects.

sections.text: French Justice Minister Gérald Darmanin said on Friday that 232 people have been jailed over the looting and attacks on police of 17 and 18 October, up from 217 on Thursday [10][13]. He said 1,144 people have been referred to prosecutors, prosecutors have opened 263 cases on organised-gang charges, and more than 100 judicial investigations are under way [10]. Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said nearly 500 people have been arrested through follow-up investigations since 17 October [10]. The Justice Ministry counts 2,700 people taken into custody since last Saturday, Al Jazeera reported, with AFP [14]. Darmanin said trials of those behind the worst violence will continue in the coming weeks [10].
Confidence is high, because the figures come from the two ministers on record, relayed by CNews and matched by Euronews and AFP; they are official counts not independently confirmed.

items.title: Italian Truckers Lift Most Southern Blockades Ahead of 27 October Talks
items.lede: Fuel stations in Campania still ran dry and a grocery chain head said Italy needs three to seven days to restock fresh food.

sections.text: Hauliers in Italy removed blockades in Campania, Calabria, Puglia, and Basilicata on Friday, with some pickets left in Naples, Corriere della Sera reported [15]. ANSA said deliveries to supermarkets resumed in Calabria as the protest waits for a 27 October meeting at the Transport Ministry [16]. Transport Minister Matteo Salvini said on 22 October that hauliers' leasing payments would be suspended until the end of March 2027, ANSA reported [17]. Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni called the remaining roadblocks 'intimidation' and said the government would use the law making road blocking a crime [17], and Justice Minister Carlo Nordio said mafia infiltration of the protests was 'highly probable' [18]. Many fuel stations in Campania were sold out, and the head of the Conad chain told ANSA a return to normal will take three to seven days, with fruit, vegetables, fish, and meat hit hardest [15]. Taxi unions plan a fuel-cost protest in Rome on 26 October [15]. The government put average self-service prices on Friday at 2.022 euros a litre for petrol and 2.260 for diesel [15].

Confidence is high, because Corriere della Sera and ANSA report the lifting and the ministers spoke on record; Nordio's view is his own assessment; the ANSA page was read only in part behind a consent wall.

items.title: Brussels Bans Shared Scooters From Its Centre Ahead of Belgian Weekend Protests
items.lede: The city acted after fresh calls for a Saturday march, recalling that rental scooters were wrecked and torched in earlier unrest, and Liège hotels report weekend cancellations.

sections.text: Brussels Mobility in Belgium said shared electric scooters and bikes will be barred from the Pentagon, the capital's historic centre, from 10:00 on Friday to 22:00 on Saturday [19][20]. The ban follows new calls for a city-centre protest on Saturday, after shared scooters were often wrecked and set on fire in earlier protests [20]. In Liège, hoteliers reported about 700 cancellations for the coming weekend, saying people do not feel safe because of the protests [20]. No police estimate of Saturday's turnout was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is high on the ban, because Brussels Mobility announced it and Belga and VRT report it. The Liège cancellation figure rests on hoteliers quoted by VRT.

items.title: Netherlands Shuts Its Cairo Embassy After Nine Days of Protests
items.lede: Demonstrators are demanding the release of an Egyptian official held by Dutch police since 10 October, and the mission must be evacuated at each protest.

sections.text: The Dutch embassy in Egypt reported nine straight days of protests over the arrest in the Netherlands of Ahmed Nasser, a pro-government Egyptian youth official [21]. The embassy said on Facebook it had to be evacuated during every protest, NOS reported, and it is closed until further notice [21]. Dutch police arrested Nasser on 10 October, reportedly for threatening the activist Anas Habib, and his pre-trial detention was extended by 14 days [21]. NOS said protesters were bussed daily to the embassy in Zamalek, a rare sight under Egypt's restrictions on protest [21]. Egypt's foreign minister had asked Dutch Foreign Minister Berendsen for Nasser's release a day after the arrest [21]. No Egyptian government comment on the closure was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate, because one major Dutch outlet reports the closure, citing the embassy's own statement. An Anadolu report could not be reached.

theaters.heading: Security, politics, and Russian pressure on Estonia, Latvia, and Lithuania

items.title: Estonian Military Intelligence Says Putin Inflates Russia's Battlefield Gains in Ukraine
items.lede: Intelligence chief Ants Kiviselg put Russian losses at about 1,900 troops a day, with weekly losses above 10,000 for an eighth straight week.

sections.text: Ants Kiviselg, head of the Estonian Defense Forces Intelligence Center, told his weekly press conference that Russia's leadership consistently portrays the war in Ukraine more favourably than reality, citing Vladimir Putin's 16 October claim of 310 settlements and 6,500 square kilometres captured this year, ERR News reported [1]. He said an average of 240 combat engagements took place daily, heaviest on the Pokrovsk and Kostiantynivka axes in Donetsk Oblast [1]. Kiviselg said Russia's inaccurate portrayal of the line of contact could become a point of contention in any ceasefire talks, and that Moscow's efforts to shape perceptions of the front are cognitive warfare [1]. ERR said reports also emerged during the week of potentially hostile Russian satellite activity in space [1].
Confidence is high that Estonia's intelligence chief made these assessments, which ERR reports directly; the loss and engagement figures are Estonian estimates and were not independently checked.

items.title: Estonian Prosecutors Close Auvere Power Plant Drone Case Without Finding Origin
items.lede: Investigators even asked Ukrainian experts whether a stray Ukrainian drone hit the smokestack, but the wreckage was too badly destroyed to tell.

sections.text: Estonia's Prosecutor's Office has closed its criminal investigation into the drone that struck a smokestack at the Auvere Power Plant near the Russian border at 03:43 on 25 March, ERR News reported on 23 October [2]. State Prosecutor Gardi Anderson said the drone was so extensively destroyed in the collision and explosion that its origin could not be reliably determined, and that the case can be reopened if new evidence emerges [2]. The Internal Security Service (KAPO) said the information gathered did not indicate a deliberate act directed against Estonia, and Deputy Director General Andres Ratassepp warned that more such incidents should be expected while Russia's war against Ukraine continues [2]. The strike damaged the smokestack but injured no one and did not disrupt the power system [2].
Confidence is high on the closure and the officials' statements, because ERR quotes the prosecutor and KAPO directly; no prosecutor's office release was read.

items.title: Herem Expects Sharp Rise in Russian Threat Once Ukraine War Ends
items.lede: Estonia's new defence minister wants faster preparations, stronger air defences, and a public that understands the risks and how to respond.

sections.text: Estonian Defense Minister Martin Herem told ERR in an interview published on 23 October that the threat from Russia will increase dramatically from the moment it stops using its current resources in Ukraine [3]. He said he has set out that updated threat assessment at the Ministry of Defense, though he said it has not yet been formulated at government level or put on paper [3]. Herem said Estonia must accelerate defence preparations and strengthen air defences, adding that the country is not entering the drone warfare era completely barehanded [3]. The interview follows former ministry secretary general Kaimo Kuusk's claim that Herem cited a very different perception of the threat as the reason they could not keep working together; Herem said he would not describe anything as impossible [3].
Confidence is high on what Herem said, because ERR publishes the interview; the threat assessment itself is not public.

items.title: Lithuanian Companies Supply Metal Nets to Guard Strategic Sites from Drones
items.lede: The push follows the 18 October drone incursion, and one maker says its nets already cover some sites but would not name them.

sections.text: Lithuanian firms are producing anti-drone netting to protect the country's strategic objects, LRT reported on 23 October, citing the business daily Verslo Žinios [4]. Alvydas Pundzius of the company Kovas confirmed that its metal nets already protect some strategic objects but declined to give details [4]. Lithuania decided to increase anti-drone protection of strategic objects after the 18 October drone incursion, Verslo Žinios reported [4]. No Lithuanian government statement on the netting was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate, because LRT relays a single newspaper report and the company declined to give details.

items.title: Latvian Border Guards Find 13 Migrants in Smugglers' Car Far from Belarus
items.lede: Two Ukrainian drivers face people-smuggling charges, adding to 168 such criminal cases the State Border Guard has opened this year.

sections.text: Acting on a tip-off, Latvia's State Border Guard stopped a Volkswagen on a highway near Valmiera, in the north of the country, and found 13 people without valid documents who had illegally crossed the Belarusian-Latvian border, LSM reported on 23 October [5]. The driver and passenger, both Ukrainian citizens, face criminal proceedings for people smuggling and were themselves in Latvia without valid papers [5]. LSM noted that the location, far from the Belarus border, suggests the group may have been heading north towards Estonia or Finland rather than south towards Germany [5]. The State Border Guard has opened 168 criminal proceedings against 119 people this year for such offences [5].
Confidence is high on the stop and the case count, which LSM attributes to the State Border Guard; the route is LSM's inference.

items.title: Lithuania's Finance Minister Says Coalition Partners Pushed for Deep Defence Cuts
items.lede: Taurimas Valys says the government held defence spending above 5% of GDP despite a sizeable deficit and pressure to match the US minimum.

sections.text: Lithuanian Finance Minister Taurimas Valys told LRT.lt in an interview published on 23 October that there was considerable pressure, including from coalition partners, to sharply reduce defence spending while preparing next year's budget [6]. He said some proposed tying Lithuania to the minimum required by the United States, but the government 'stood firm' [6]. Valys said Lithuania's commitment to spend more than 5% of GDP on defence is already paying off, because investors no longer treat the country as a war zone [6]. He also faced opposition pressure, he said [6].
Confidence is high on Valys's remarks, because LRT publishes the interview; no coalition partner response was read.

theaters.heading: Stability, politics, and outside influence in the Western Balkans

items.title: Disabled Serbians Report Pressure to Back Ruling SNS Before Sunday Vote
items.lede: One woman says she was warned she might lose her care allowance, and an activist describes a widespread fear among people with disabilities.

sections.text: People with disabilities in Serbia face pressure to vote for the ruling Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) in the 25 October parliamentary election, Balkan Insight reported on 23 October [1]. A woman with a disability, speaking anonymously, said a representative of a major disability association, which depends on state or local funding, told her she 'might never receive the care allowance again' if she did not vote SNS [1]. A human rights activist described a 'collective fear', saying many vote for the ruling party even without direct threats, fearing loss of allowances they are legally entitled to [1]. No SNS or government response was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate, because the account rests on anonymous sources in one BIRN report.

items.title: Kosovo President Sends Specialist Chambers Bill Back to Parliament
items.lede: The PDK, which sponsored the law curbing the Hague-based war crimes court, itself asked Justina Shiroka Pula to let lawmakers reconsider it.

sections.text: Kosovo President Justina Shiroka Pula returned the amended Kosovo Specialist Chambers (KSC) bill to parliament on 22 October for review at the request of the Democratic Party of Kosovo (PDK), less than three weeks after its approval, Balkan Insight reported [2]. The law aims to curtail the jurisdiction of the Hague-based court and followed weeks of protests by Kosovo Liberation Army veterans after four former KLA leaders were convicted [2]. The president's office said PDK asked that the assembly reconsider the provisions on the court's jurisdiction and mandate [2]. Her statement also reiterated opposition to any attempt to cast doubt on the liberation nature of the war [2].
Confidence is high, because Balkan Insight quotes the president's office statement; the statement itself was not read.

items.title: Footage of Police Beating Teenagers Fuels Alarm over Albania's Protest Policing
items.lede: In one video a youth shouts that he is only 13 as officers swing batons, and similar clips from Tirana have spread all week.

sections.text: On 22 October, the tenth straight day of protests in Tirana, Albania, students and professors rallied outside parliament [3]. Protesters then moved to the prime minister's office, rejected Prime Minister Edi Rama's renewed offer of dialogue, and overturned concrete blocks marked 'dialogue' [4]. On 21 October masked groups threw Molotov cocktails, stones, and fireworks at police outside the prime minister's office, and police answered with water cannon and tear gas [5] [6]. State Police earlier reported 271 arrests over seven days [7][8]; the Health Ministry put injuries at 310, including 191 police officers, on 19 October, and official figures reached 320 by 21 October [9][8]. On 23 October Balkan Insight reported that a video shared on the evening of 19 October shows police officers rushing at several young people and beating them with batons, while one shouts that he is only 13 [10]. BIRN could not verify the ages, but said similar footage of Tirana police using force against protesters, including minors, has circulated widely over the past week [10]. No State Police response to the footage was found by the cutoff.

Confidence is high on the 21 October clashes and earlier counts, because RTSH, Periskopi, police, and health figures agree; confidence is moderate on the footage, which Balkan Insight could not fully verify.

items.title: Belgrade Rally Draws About 150,000 as Serbia Enters Election Silence
items.lede: Campaigning is now banned until polls close at 20:00 on Sunday, with about 6.45 million Serbians choosing among 18 lists for 250 seats.

sections.text: About 150,000 supporters of Serbia's student-led movement rallied around Slavija Square in central Belgrade on 22 October, the last campaign day before the 25 October snap parliamentary election, AFP reported via the Guardian [11]. The Student List seeks to end more than 14 years of rule by Aleksandar Vučić's SNS, which he now leads as a candidate after stepping down as president [11] [12]. Civil society groups say the campaign was marred by intimidation, arrests, and misuse of public resources [11]; PACE described a 'tense and divisive electoral climate', and CRTA warned of threats and physical violence [13]. The legal campaign silence began at midnight and bans promoting candidates, calls to vote, and publishing result estimates until polls close, with fines up to RSD 600,000 [14] [12]. Serbia's 6,450,523 registered voters will use 8,392 polling stations, 93 of them abroad in 37 countries [14]. The Guardian notes that media bias and voter-list irregularities mean any result could be contested [15].

Confidence is high on the rally, the silence rules, and the voter figures, because the Guardian, BTA, and Serbia's public broadcaster RTS report them consistently; the crowd size is AFP's figure, carried by the Guardian.

items.title: Belgrade Court Orders Custody for Five in Alleged Serbian Election-Day Riot Plot
items.lede: Those held include a Croatian and a Bosnian citizen, and prosecutors say the alleged ringleader planned to bring about 80 people to Belgrade on Sunday.

sections.text: Serbian police arrested five people aged 27 and 28 in Novi Sad on 21 October, and Belgrade prosecutors said they planned violence, riots, and attacks on opponents and police on the 25 October election day, Balkan Insight and BBC Serbian reported [16] [17]. Prosecutors said the group planned mobile teams with balaclavas, poles, flares, knives, and weapons to travel to Belgrade, and one suspect was to command about 40 people [16] [17]. A Belgrade activist of the group Belgrade Stays and a Student List supporter in Vrnjačka Banja were also detained; their lawyer and a local coordinator said searches found nothing but campaign material [16] [17]. On 22 October Belgrade's Higher Court ordered custody for five suspects, a Croatian, a Bosnian, and three Serbian citizens, while a sixth suspect, a woman, was released by prosecutors, Euronews Srbija reported citing Tanjug [18]. Most suspects stayed silent at questioning; prosecutors allege the leader expected to command 80 to 90 people and planned arson and Molotov attacks [18]. The ages Tanjug gives differ from earlier reports.
Confidence is high on the arrests and moderate on the custody order, which rests on Euronews Srbija's Tanjug-based report alone; the plot allegations come from prosecutors and are untested.

items.title: Merz Urges Kosovo and Serbia to Revive Dialogue at Montenegro Summit
items.lede: Kosovo's Albin Kurti pressed for an account of more than 1,500 missing persons as Montenegro closed its term chairing the Berlin Process.

sections.text: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz called for immediate progress in the Kosovo–Serbia dialogue at the Berlin Process leaders' summit in Miločer, near Budva, Montenegro, on 22 October, Albeu reported [19]; Montenegrin Prime Minister Milojko Spajić opened the summit that morning [20]. Merz urged Pristina and Belgrade to avoid escalation and rhetoric that fuels conflict, saying 'we must not pour gasoline on the fire' [19]. Kosovo Prime Minister Albin Kurti demanded justice for war crimes, an account of more than 1,500 missing persons, and cited 23 Albanian bodies recently exhumed in Zubin Potok [19]. The summit ends Montenegro's chairmanship of the process [19]. North Macedonia's Prime Minister Hristijan Mickoski said he expected strong messages on EU integration, as his country's accession talks have still not begun [21].
Confidence is moderate, because one regional outlet reports the remarks; no German government transcript was read.

theaters.heading: Stability, politics, and outside influence in the South Caucasus

items.title: Russia's Grushko Calls South Caucasus an EU Arena for Confronting Moscow
items.lede: The deputy foreign minister says Brussels makes would-be members give up their independence by aligning with statements mostly aimed at Russia.

sections.text: Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Alexander Grushko said the European Union treats the South Caucasus as an arena of confrontation with Russia, NEWS.am reported on 23 October, citing RIA Novosti [1]. Grushko said countries seeking EU membership or candidacy are pressured to give up their independence before joining, because the EU requires them to align with its common foreign and security policy statements, 80 percent of which concern Russia [1]. He did not name Armenia or Georgia in the remarks quoted [1]. No EU response was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate, because the quote reaches L24 through NEWS.am citing Russian state agency RIA Novosti; the original was not read.

items.title: Georgian Ex-Deputy Minister Mikautadze Sees Ten-Year Term Cut to Three
items.lede: The plea deal follows his testimony against jailed former security chief Grigol Liluashvili and includes a GEL 1 million fine and asset seizures.

sections.text: Georgia's Prosecutor's Office said on 23 October that former First Deputy Economy Minister Romeo Mikautadze, sentenced to ten years for abuse of office and money laundering, had his term reduced to three years plus a two-year suspended sentence under a plea agreement approved by Tbilisi's Court of Appeals, Civil.ge reported [2]. He was fined GEL 1 million, barred from public office for three years, and will lose assets worth GEL 5.54 million, including an apartment in Madrid, Spain [2]. Prosecutors had said Mikautadze testified that he facilitated a bribe for former State Security Service chief Grigol Liluashvili, later jailed for 13 years [2].
Confidence is high, because Civil.ge quotes the Prosecutor's Office statement.

items.title: Armenian Anti-Graft Body Charges 24 over Vote Buying Before Stepanavan Poll
items.lede: Investigators say the bribes were meant to win votes for the opposition Strong Armenia party, whose mayoral candidate is now in pretrial detention.

sections.text: Armenia's Anti-Corruption Committee arrested ten more people on 23 October in a vote-buying case in the northern city of Stepanavan, bringing the number charged to 24, NEWS.am reported [3]. Those held face charges of giving, aiding, and receiving election bribes to secure votes for the opposition Strong Armenia party's candidate in Sunday's municipal election [3]. The Anti-Corruption Court placed Arsen Gevorgyan, Strong Armenia's mayoral candidate in Stepanavan, in pretrial detention for two months [3]. No Strong Armenia response was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate, because one outlet relays the committee's account and the charges are untested.

items.title: Aliyev Hosts India's Jaishankar as New Delhi Backs Peace with Armenia
items.lede: The Indian minister came on Prime Minister Modi's instructions, and both sides stressed shared Global South positions on international issues.

sections.text: Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev received Indian External Affairs Minister Subrahmanyam Jaishankar in Baku on 23 October, the presidential website said [4]. Jaishankar said he was visiting on Prime Minister Narendra Modi's instructions, and the two sides discussed political, trade, high-tech, and cultural cooperation and shared Global South positions [4]. Jaishankar said India welcomes the peace agreements Azerbaijan and Armenia reached in August last year and wants disputes settled through dialogue and diplomacy, NEWS.am reported [5].
Confidence is high on the meeting and the remarks, which the Azerbaijani presidency and NEWS.am report.

items.title: Poland Holds Second Georgian Suspect in Killing of Anti-Putin Cartoonist
items.lede: A court ordered three months' custody for the 22-year-old, accused of aiding the June shooting of artist Robert Kuzovkov near Belarus.

sections.text: Poland's Internal Security Agency (ABW) detained a 22-year-old Georgian citizen, named as Makhmud A, on suspicion of aiding and abetting the murder of Russian satirical artist Robert Kuzovkov, Polish special services coordinator Tomasz Siemoniak announced on 22 October, Civil.ge and OC Media reported [6] [7]. The National Prosecutor's Office said he was detained on 19 October in a car park on the A2 motorway [7]. Kuzovkov, known as Semyon Skrepetsky for cartoons mocking Vladimir Putin and Ramzan Kadyrov, was shot dead in Biała Podlaska on 15 June [6] [7]. He had reported death threats from Kadyrov supporters [7]. An earlier suspect held in June was using a Georgian passport [6].
Confidence is high, because two outlets report Siemoniak's statement consistently; the allegations are untested in court.

items.title: Two Georgians Held Since 2024 Near Tskhinvali Line Return Home
items.lede: Georgia's security service credits the EU monitors' hotline and raised the killing of Tamaz Ginturi at same-day incident talks in Ergneti.

sections.text: Georgia's State Security Service (SSSG) said on 22 October that two Georgian citizens detained on 16 September 2024 near Mejvriskhevi, by the occupation line of Russia-occupied Tskhinvali/South Ossetia, had been released and returned to Tbilisi-controlled territory, Civil.ge reported [8]. The SSSG said it used all instruments available, including the EU Monitoring Mission's hotline, and did not name the two [8]. The same day, the 135th Incident Prevention and Response Mechanism meeting in Ergneti, co-facilitated by the EUMM and the OSCE, discussed recent incidents [9]. The Georgian side demanded justice for the killing of Georgian citizen Tamaz Ginturi by Russian forces, condemned borderisation, and demanded the release of everyone still held [9].
Confidence is high on the release and the meeting, because Civil.ge relays SSSG statements; no de facto Tskhinvali account was read.

items.title: Russian Judge Named De Facto Premier of Georgia's Occupied South Ossetia
items.lede: Soslan Margiev chaired a court near Moscow until this year, and a native of Russia was named his first deputy days earlier.

sections.text: Marat Kambolov, declared winner of the September de facto 'presidential' vote in Georgia's Russia-occupied Tskhinvali/South Ossetia region, appointed Soslan Margiev de facto 'prime minister' on 22 October after the region's 'parliament' unanimously approved him, Civil.ge reported [10]. Margiev worked in Russia's judicial system for more than 20 years, including as chairman of the Lobnya City Court in the Moscow Region from 2022 to 2026 [10]. On 19 October Kambolov named Ekaterina Tolstikova, a native of Russia, first deputy 'chairman of the government' [10]. Emilia Gagieva was also reapproved as head of the region's election commission [10].
Confidence is high on the appointments, which Civil.ge reports from de facto decrees; no Georgian government reaction was read.

items.title: Armenian Court Keeps Kocharyan's Son Sedrak in Custody Two More Months
items.lede: Former President Robert Kocharyan is held in the same state-property case.

sections.text: Armenia's Anti-Corruption Court extended the pretrial detention of Sedrak Kocharyan, eldest son of former President Robert Kocharyan, by two months, Armenpress and NEWS.am reported on 23 October, the latter citing lawyer Hakob Kyureghyan [11] [12]. He has been held since 26 August on charges of large-scale money laundering and aiding abuse of office and bribe-taking [11]. The Anti-Corruption Committee says state properties, including the Play City centre and Kaputak Sevan resort, were sold below market value to people tied to the former president during his term [11]. Both deny wrongdoing [11]. Former President Robert Kocharyan is also in pre-trial detention in the same case [11].
Confidence is high on the son's extension, which Armenpress and NEWS.am report.

items.title: Nearly Two in Three Germans Back Military Help for Ukraine, ZDF Survey Finds
items.lede: Support splits sharply by party and region: 81 percent of AfD backers want cuts, and the eastern states back the aid only narrowly, at 49 percent.

sections.text: In the ZDF Politbarometer, 30 percent of Germans want more military support for Ukraine, 33 percent want it kept at today's level, and 32 percent want less [1]. Support is highest among Green (89 percent) and CDU/CSU (83 percent) supporters, while 81 percent of AfD supporters want cuts [1]. In eastern Germany a narrow 49 percent back the aid against 42 percent for reductions, compared with 67 percent support in the west [1]. Asked whether Putin will attack NATO's eastern members or the Baltic states, 46 percent expect it and 48 percent do not [1]. The same survey puts the AfD at 26 percent (down two) and the CDU/CSU at 23 percent (up two), with the SPD at 14, Greens 13, Left 11, and FDP 3 percent [2]. Forschungsgruppe Wahlen polled 1,225 eligible voters by phone and online from 20 to 22 October, with a margin of error of two to three points [2].
Confidence is high on the poll figures, because two outlets report the same ZDF survey. A single poll measures stated opinion within its error margin and is not a forecast.

items.title: Leaked Emails Challenge Weidel's Account of Illegal Swiss Donations to the AfD
items.lede: A July 2017 email bearing her sender ID says donations had been announced to her, contradicting her claim she learned of the 132,000 euros only weeks later.

sections.text: Leaked internal emails of Germany's far-right AfD suggest party leader Alice Weidel knew earlier than she has said about illegal campaign donations from Switzerland, Der Spiegel reported on Friday [3]. WDR and NDR found a July 2017 email bearing Weidel's sender ID telling two confidants that donations had been 'announced' to her to fund her social-media campaign and asking that the account be watched for incoming payments [4]. In 2017, 132,000 euros arrived in 18 instalments on her district association's account, nominally from a Swiss pharmaceutical firm; the payments were later ruled illegal, and the AfD paid a fine of almost 400,000 euros [4]. Weidel said at the time she learned of the money weeks after it arrived and was 'surprised' [4]. Prosecutors ended their investigation in 2021 without proof of collusion with the donor, and the emails come from an illegal hack [4]. No response from Weidel or the AfD was found by the cutoff.

Confidence is moderate on the email content, because it rests on media reporting of hacked material whose authenticity has not been publicly confirmed by the AfD. Confidence is high on the 2017 donation facts and the fine, which are long on record.

items.title: Baden-Württemberg Drafts Civilian Home Defence Plan Mirroring Germany's Military Blueprint
items.lede: The interior minister wants police, soldiers, towns, and utilities to train together, citing over 30 billion euros in 2025 losses to cyberattacks, spying, and sabotage.

sections.text: Baden-Württemberg Interior Minister Manuel Hagel (CDU) announced what he called the largest overhaul of the southwestern German state's security architecture, at a forum with the Bundeswehr state command at the Stuttgart trade fair [5]. He said the state will be the first to build a home defence plan that mirrors the military 'Operationsplan Deutschland' on the civilian side, with police, Bundeswehr, municipalities, civil protection, and critical-infrastructure operators planning and training together [5]. A home defence directorate and a cyber situation centre are to be set up in the Interior Ministry, and he wants the state's domestic intelligence office to disrupt networks, not only observe them [5]. Hagel cited a suspected attack on a Reutlingen substation, said 'we are in Russia's crosshairs', put 2025 damage from cyberattacks, espionage, and sabotage in the state at over 30 billion euros, and counted more than 20,000 extremists [5]. No timetable or cost was reported.
Confidence is high that Hagel made these announcements, because dpa quotes him directly. The figures are his and were not independently checked; only one report was found.

items.title: Wadephul Joins Seven Ministers in Istanbul to Defend Free Shipping Lanes
items.lede: Berlin and Ankara convened the first meeting of this group, where Germany accused Iran and the Houthis of blackmailing world trade and Russia of starving the Global South.

sections.text: Germany's Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul (CDU) met his counterparts from France, Britain, Italy, Turkey, Egypt, Pakistan, and Saudi Arabia in Istanbul on Friday, the first meeting in this format, held at German and Turkish initiative [6] [7]. Italy's presence widens the European side beyond the three countries named by Berlin sources on Thursday [6] [8]. The Foreign Office said the focus was freedom of navigation and the conflicts in Iran and Yemen, noting that about 12 percent of world maritime trade passes the Bab al-Mandab and about a fifth of global oil the Strait of Hormuz [6]. Wadephul said the eight countries reject Iran and the Houthi militia 'blackmailing world trade' and accused Moscow of knowingly accepting food shortages in the Global South through attacks on Black Sea grain shipments [7] [6]. The German Shipowners' Association (VDR) welcomed the initiative, saying Germany must not be a bystander on sea-lane security [7]. No joint statement from the eight ministers was found by the cutoff.

Confidence is high that the meeting took place with these eight countries, because the German Foreign Office and Reuters report it. Confidence is high on Wadephul's quoted positions, which come from his own ministry. No outcome document was available.

items.title: German Judge Orders Ukrainian Spy Suspect Held in Pretrial Custody
items.lede: Prosecutors allege the man gathered data on tank, ammunition, and explosives output and on NATO eastern-flank sites for Russian intelligence since at least July 2025.

sections.text: An investigating judge at Germany's Federal Court of Justice on Friday put into effect the arrest warrant against Ukrainian national Vadym Y., so he stays in pretrial detention, the Federal Prosecutor said [9] [10]. Federal police (BKA) had arrested him in the Oder-Spree district of Brandenburg on Thursday [11] [12]. Prosecutors say he was in contact with a Russian intelligence service through an intermediary since at least July 2025 and gathered information on production of armoured vehicles, ammunition, and explosives, and on personnel and military sites securing NATO's eastern flank [11]. Some of it was public; for the rest he allegedly pumped contacts in the European defence industry [11]. The case began with a tip from the domestic intelligence service [11]. Chancellor Friedrich Merz said Russian intelligence activity in Germany remains 'unchanged high' [10]. The prosecutor gave no further detail on the eastern-flank allegations, and no comment from Kyiv or Moscow was found by the cutoff [10].

Confidence is high on the arrest, the detention order, and the allegations as stated, because they come from the prosecutor's own statements and are reported by the Stuttgarter Zeitung and Al Jazeera. The allegations are unproven and no charge has been filed.

items.title: AfD Stays Ahead at 27 Percent as Union Narrows Gap in German Poll
items.lede: The FDP falls to 4 percent, below the Bundestag threshold, while the SPD and Greens tie at 14 percent in the survey of 1,048 voters.

sections.text: An Allensbach survey for the Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung puts the far-right AfD at 27 percent in Germany's national vote intention, one point lower than in September and two points higher than in January [13] [14]. Chancellor Merz's CDU/CSU is unchanged at 23 percent but four points below January [13]. The SPD rose one point to 14 percent, level with the Greens, the Left gained a point to 11 percent, and the FDP slipped from 5 to 4 percent [13] [14]. dpa noted that the Union's share is higher than other institutes show, where it has fallen below 20 percent, so the AfD's lead here is markedly smaller [14]. Allensbach questioned 1,048 people between 2 and 16 October, with a margin of error of about three points for a 30 percent share [14].
Confidence is high on the poll figures, because the commissioning newspaper and dpa report the same numbers. A single poll measures stated intention within its error margin and is not a forecast.
